description.narrative:
Stakeholder effects Increased access to finance for MSMEs. The Project will support KMF, the largest microfinance institution in the country, in growing its reach to microentrepreneurs and small enterprises, including agricultural and women-owned businesses.
Stakeholder effects Improved access and quality of financial services for MSMEs and consumers: KMF leverages a unique sales model targeting micro and small entrepreneurs from rural areas, involving special agents who regularly travel to clients' places of business. The project will support KMFs effort to capitalize on this competitive advantage compared to incumbent banks and digital innovators, by helping the company transform into a bank and develop a suite of financial products, including transaction and deposit accounts, digital banking and payment tools, to help increase the penetration of financial services amongst its clients.
Contribution to Market Creation - Competitiveness: IFC anticipates that the combination of this Project and its associated advisory engagement will foster competitiveness among financial providers in Kazakhstan by helping the largest MFI in the market transform into a bank and begin offering a variety of credit and non-credit products and services to a clientele traditionally underserved by the banking sector.

The Project involves a senior loan of up to US$50 million in US Dollars from IFCs own account and may include a senior syndicated loan, for on-lending to micro and small enterprises, including women-owned enterprises and agri-business enterprises.
